clue.text: Challenging attitude of French engaged one

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a fiancé is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's fiancé shows a defiant streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance is a bold, resisting stance, an attitude that challenges authority.

clue.text: Cry when second best

parts.note: the cream is the best part of anything, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out on finishing runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud, piercing shout, a kind of cry.

clue.text: Foreign, ergo must they have superior taste?

definitions.text: Foreign, ergo must they have superior taste?

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or alien, so these letters are made strange by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry question: are foreigners therefore the ones with refined palates?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the rearranged letters are people who, the clue asks, have superior taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Gourmets are connoisseurs of fine food and drink, people with refined palates.

clue.text: Egyptian symbol made a mark on sailor

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so the mark comes first

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a crossword sailor

explanation.surface: An Egyptian emblem has left a mark on a seaman's skin, like a tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was a sacred emblem in ancient Egypt, common on amulets and seals.

clue.text: Give advice to everyone on publicity

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on after another, so everyone follows publicity

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity work
each means every one taken individually

explanation.surface: Advising all and sundry by means of advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to urge moral counsel on others, giving advice, often unwanted.

clue.text: Feeble grasp of chapter that's hard-hitting

indicators.note: the feeble word holds the chapter letters in its grip

parts.note: puny means weak or feeble

explanation.surface: A weak grasp of a book's chapter seems an odd thing to call forceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Punchy describes something forceful and effective, like a punch landing.

clue.text: Compelled daughter to join police

indicators.note: the daughter's letter joins on at the end of the police

parts.note: the police force, or simply the force

explanation.surface: A daughter was made to sign up with the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced means made to act against one's will, the same as obliged.

clue.text: Routines are boring!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: practised exercises or routines
second meaning: tools that drill are boring holes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface complains that routine is dull; the second sense is boring as making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both repeated training exercises and tools or actions that pierce holes.

clue.text: They're a sign that something's missing

definitions.meaning: reads like a warning signal or omen; in fact a punctuation mark
sounds like a loss; in fact the letters dropped in a contraction such as they're

explanation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates itself: they're and something's each contain the punctuation mark that shows letters left out.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark shows where letters have been omitted, as in can't or it's.

clue.text: I'd even dressed some salad leaves

indicators.note: salad is dressed by tossing it, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having even put dressing on some salad greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' fits the salad so well it seems part of the picture, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy chicory plant whose bitter leaves are used in salads.

clue.text: Crazy patriot gets right in the picture

indicators.note: the right letter goes into the middle of the scrambled word
crazy means wild or deranged, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mad nationalist finds himself correctly placed in the frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or photograph of a person, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Insubstantial vessel gets hot inside

indicators.note: the hot letter sits within the vessel word

parts.note: a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: A flimsy container heats up within.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin means lacking substance or weight, as in a thin excuse.

clue.text: Dance like the Lone Ranger?

definitions.meaning: the Lone Ranger, a Western hero, always wore a mask over his eyes

explanation.walkthrough: The Lone Ranger was a masked cowboy hero of radio, TV and film, so a dance in his style has everyone masked.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade ball is a dance where guests wear masks, as the cowboy hero did.

clue.text: Big cat's family hide when spotted

parts.note: a leopard is a big cat; the possessive gives its trailing s
kin means one's relatives or family

explanation.surface: A big cat's relatives take cover when they are seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide and spotted look like verbs about being seen; they mean a pelt and dappled.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopardskin is the spotted pelt of the animal, a hide covered in rosette markings.

clue.text: Father and children take in good music

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the children word takes the good letter into its middle

parts.note: sons are male children

explanation.surface: Dad and the kids enjoy some decent tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop songs are popular chart music, short catchy tracks.

clue.text: Demonstrate how I acted in plays

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor shows off the stage roles in their career.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays looks like the theatre works the actor appeared in; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or show, so it can mean demonstrate.

clue.text: Adjust the sum of money left

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to alter or modify
second meaning: the money returned after paying more than the price

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as fixing an account balance; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for altering something and a noun for coins handed back after a purchase.

clue.text: The mark of an oarsman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single line made by a pen or brush
second meaning: in a rowing eight

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the sign of a good rower; the stroke is also the rower nearest the stern, whom the others follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pen line and the pace-setting member of a rowing crew.

clue.text: Government report gets mixed up with the last exam

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last means take just the final letter of the following word

parts.note: only the final letter of this word is used
an exam paper is the test sheet itself

explanation.surface: An official report gets confused with the final test a student sat.
explanation.walkthrough: The last exam sounds like a final test; last applies only to the.
explanation.definitionFit: A white paper is a government policy document laying out proposals before legislation.

clue.text: Link communist with rows

parts.note: to tie is to link or bind
red is the colour of communism, and a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: Someone connects a party Red to rows of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered means arranged in tiers, ascending layers such as rows of seats.

clue.text: Have fun taking in a show

indicators.note: the fun word takes the letter a into its middle

parts.note: to revel is to make merry
taken as written, the single letter

explanation.surface: Enjoying yourself by going to see a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Show looks like a noun for a performance; it is the verb to disclose.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to make visible or disclose, which is to show.

clue.text: Points to girl next to son

indicators.note: the son letter is placed alongside the girl

parts.note: Dot is a girl's name, short for Dorothy

explanation.surface: Someone gestures toward a girl standing beside a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dots are small round marks, points such as full stops.

clue.text: Covering letter

definitions.meaning: read as an adjective it describes a note sent with a document; really it means wrapping round
the item of post being wrapped

explanation.walkthrough: A covering letter is a note sent with an application; read differently, it is the thing that covers a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is the paper wrapper a letter is posted in.

clue.text: Winner has a comic name

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a long-running British boys' comic

explanation.walkthrough: The Victor was a British weekly comic of war and sports stories, running from 1961 to 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor is the one who triumphs, and the word was also the title of a British comic paper.

clue.text: Appear at one point to come together

parts.note: E, east, is one point of the compass
to merge is to combine or come together

explanation.surface: Things show up at the place where they meet.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, which is to appear.

clue.text: Chap conceals books in cloak

indicators.note: the chap word hides the books inside itself

parts.note: a chap is a man, a male
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A man hides books under his cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a loose sleeveless cape, a kind of cloak.
